title: MATH GAOKAO - 428
description: Authentic-style mathematics problems inspired by China’s Gaokao — build deeper understanding, sharper thinking, and real exam readiness.

questions.learningObjective: Simplify a linear expression by distributing and combining like terms.
questions.question: Simplify \(3(2x-4)-2(x-5)\).
questions.explanation: Distribute: \(3(2x-4)=6x-12\) and \(-2(x-5)=-2x+10\). Then \(6x-12-2x+10=(6x-2x)+(-12+10)=4x-2\). Thus the simplified expression is \(4x-2\).
questions.hint: Distribute each product first, then combine the \(x\)-terms and the constant terms.

questions.learningObjective: Solve a linear equation involving fractions by clearing denominators.
questions.question: Solve \(\frac{2x-1}{3}+\frac{x+2}{2}=4\).
questions.hint: Multiply the entire equation by the least common denominator \(6\) to eliminate the fractions.

questions.learningObjective: Find the roots of a quadratic equation by factoring.
questions.question: Solve \(x^2-7x+12=0\).
questions.explanation: Factor: \(x^2-7x+12=(x-3)(x-4)\). Setting each factor to zero gives \(x-3=0\) or \(x-4=0\), so \(x=3\) or \(x=4\).
questions.hint: Look for two numbers whose product is \(12\) and whose sum is \(-7\).

questions.learningObjective: Expand a product of binomial conjugates using the difference of squares identity.
questions.question: Expand \((2x-3)(2x+3)\).
questions.hint: Recognize the product of conjugates and apply the difference of squares identity.

questions.learningObjective: Solve a linear inequality, including reversing the inequality when dividing by a negative number.
questions.question: Solve \(-3x+5>11\).
questions.explanation: Subtract \(5\) from both sides: \(-3x>6\). Divide both sides by \(-3\); since \(-3<0\), reverse the inequality sign: \(x<-2\).
questions.hint: Remember that dividing or multiplying an inequality by a negative number reverses the inequality sign.

questions.learningObjective: Solve an absolute value equation by considering both cases.
questions.question: Solve \(|2x-1|=7\).
questions.hint: Split the absolute value equation into two separate linear equations.

questions.learningObjective: Solve a system of two linear equations in two variables.
questions.question:
Solve the system:
\[
\begin{cases}
2x+y=7,\\
x-y=2.
\end{cases}
\]
questions.explanation: From \(x-y=2\), we have \(y=x-2\). Substitute into \(2x+y=7\): \(2x+(x-2)=7\), so \(3x-2=7\), \(3x=9\), and \(x=3\). Then \(y=3-2=1\). The solution is \((3,1)\).
questions.hint: Use substitution by expressing one variable in terms of the other from the simpler equation.

questions.learningObjective: Simplify an algebraic expression involving powers using exponent rules.
questions.question: For \(a\ne 0\), simplify \(\frac{(2a^3)^2}{4a^4}\).
questions.hint: Apply the power rule to the numerator, then divide the coefficients and subtract the exponents of \(a\).

questions.learningObjective: Determine the value of a parameter for which a linear equation has no solution.
questions.question: For what value of \(k\) does the equation \(kx+3=2x+7\) have no solution?
questions.explanation: Rewrite the equation: \(kx+3=2x+7\), so \(kx-2x=4\), i.e. \((k-2)x=4\). A linear equation \(ax=b\) has no solution when \(a=0\) and \(b\ne 0\). Here \(a=k-2\) and \(b=4\). Thus \(k-2=0\), so \(k=2\). When \(k=2\), the equation becomes \(3=7\), a contradiction, so there is no solution.
questions.hint: Collect all \(x\)-terms on one side and then consider when the coefficient of \(x\) becomes zero while the constant term is nonzero.

questions.learningObjective: Simplify a rational expression by factoring and canceling common factors.
questions.question: For \(x\ne -3\), which expression is equivalent to \(\frac{x^2-9}{x+3}\)?
questions.explanation: Factor the numerator as a difference of squares: \(x^2-9=(x-3)(x+3)\). Then \(\frac{(x-3)(x+3)}{x+3}=x-3\) for \(x\ne -3\).
questions.hint: Factor the numerator using the difference of squares, then cancel the common factor.
